newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka hospitals hit by doctors' strike.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka hospitals hit by doctors' strike.

text.p: A strike by Sri Lankan doctors on Wednesday crippled about 700 government hospitals and reduced services to emergencies only, the Government Medical Officers' Association (GMOA) said.
"We have launched a one-day token strike in protest against several salary anomalies," the association's assistant secretary Lakkumar Fernando told Reuters.
"We have asked for a redress of these anomalies, but have not got a favourable response," he said.
The association, which represents more than 4,000 of the country's 4,500 Western-qualified doctors, would consider further trade union action at a meeting later on Wednesday, Fernando said.
Thousands of patients were being turned away at government hospitals, but doctors were attending to emergencies, an official for Colombo's National Hospital said.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga said the strike was "unjustified" as the government was in the process of reviewing reported salary anomalies of doctors.

"I have to express my grave concern that a trade union of professionals such as yours has taken a decision to resort to trade union action on matters receiving the attention of the government," Kumaratunga said in a letter to the association.
